issues.body: `summary_length` is produced by Python `len(text)` and the summary is sliced with `text[:240]`, both measured in Unicode code points. Here `summaryText.length` is JavaScript UTF-16 code units. Those quantities diverge for printable astral characters such as emoji. For example, a 241-emoji sanitized summary is published as 240 emoji with `summary_length: 241`, but the browser computes `summaryText.length === 480`; `obsTruncated(480, 241)` is false, so no cut marker appears even though one character was withheld. Mixed BMP/astral text can likewise produce an incorrect hidden count. The executed-page tests cover only ASCII, so they do not detect the cross-runtime mismatch.
issues.fix_hint: Use the same counting unit on both sides. For the current Python contract, compute the displayed code-point count in JavaScript (for example `Array.from(summaryText).length`) for both the predicate and hidden-count subtraction, and add an end-to-end producer-plus-page test with astral printable characters that proves a genuinely capped summary renders the correct marker and hidden count. Alternatively, explicitly redefine and implement a common counting/slicing unit in both runtimes.
issues.title: UTF-16 length comparison hides real truncation for astral Unicode

verdict.summary: The new affordance is sound for BMP-only text, and its tests exercise the producer and rendered page without relying only on lexical assertions. However, the producer and consumer do not agree on what a character count means. Python publishes code-point counts and slices by code point, while JavaScript uses UTF-16 code-unit length. Consequently, valid printable summaries containing astral Unicode can be genuinely cut by the generator yet draw no ellipsis, preserving the silent-truncation defect this PR is meant to close. Round 1, so progress is null.
